summary: Vimy tower in the Big River district, replaced by a steel tower in 1965 and closed with the district's towers in 2001; no source describes the site today.

facts.agency: Saskatchewan Department of Natural Resources (named in the annual report cited on Canada Lookouts)
facts.status_note: Closed in 2001 with the other Big River district towers; no source describes what remains at the site.

staffing.status: Ron Hook (two years) and Lourie Booker (1987-2002) listed at Vimy on the websiteservice.ca towermen list; Robert Weal named as tower man at closing in 2001 by the Big River history

events.note: Old lookout structure replaced with a modern steel tower, per the Department of Natural Resources annual report for 1965-66 quoted on Canada Lookouts.
Lourie Booker listed for 1987 to 2002 at Vimy and Birch on the towermen list.
Robert Weal named as tower man at the time of closing; the towermen list gives Booker to 2002.
Closed in 2001 with the other Big River district towers; all were condemned in August 2001.

evidence.supports: Vimy was one of the Big River district towers, about 15 km north-east of Chitek Lake
evidence.quote: Vimy Tower is the last of the seven located approximately 15 km's N.E. of Chitek Lake.

evidence.supports: Towers were built at about fifty-mile intervals across northern Saskatchewan
evidence.quote: The Department of Natural Resources soon began constructing fire control towers at approximately fifty-mile intervals across northern Saskatchewan.

evidence.supports: Spacing chosen so tower men could reach one another by radio
evidence.quote: This distance was chosen to assure that radio contact could be made between tower men.

evidence.supports: Position of Vimy on the tower list
Old structure replaced with a modern steel tower in 1965
evidence.quote: The old lookout structure was replaced with a modern steel tower.

evidence.supports: The 1965 entry comes from the Department of Natural Resources annual report for 1965-66
evidence.quote: Department of Natural Resources Annual Report, 1965-66

evidence.supports: Big River district enlarged in 1997 and 1998
evidence.quote: In 1997 & 1998, the Big River district was enlarged to include Chitek Lake area and the Dore Lake and Green Lake areas.

evidence.supports: The district had one tower before the enlargement and seven after
evidence.quote: So, instead of having one fire tower in Big River jurisdiction we now had seven towers.

evidence.supports: Ron Hook listed for two years at Vimy Tower
Lourie Booker listed from 1987 to 2002 at Vimy and Birch
Robert Weal was tower man at closing in 2001 and worked from the Chitek Lake base on fixed-wing patrols and maintenance
evidence.quote: At the time of its closing in 2001, Robert Weal was the tower man and works out of the base in Chitek Lake doing fixed-wing patrols and maintenance work at Chitek Base.

evidence.supports: Safety concerns led to the condemnation of all Big River district towers in August 2001, and tower men were given other duties
evidence.quote: There were safety concerns as to the reliability of these towers and so in August of 2001 all fire towers in the Big River district were condemned and all tower men were given alternate duties including fixed-wing patrol

Firetowers of Saskatchewan: Firetowermen and Women

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The websiteservice.ca towermen list names Ron Hook and Lourie Booker at Vimy, while the Big River history names Robert Weal as tower man when it closed in 2001. The story gives each name and does not pick one account.

notes_for_editor: The brief's agency (Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency) is not named in any fetched source; facts use the Department of Natural Resources from the annual-report citations. The jkcc page says the 1996 fire-suppression side of the Big River district was under 'Sask. Environment', which is not used. The jkcc history spells the name 'Laurie Booker'; the towermen list spells it 'Lourie'. The 1965 replacement is the only build-related fact; no source gives the original tower's date or height. The 2001 closure is not evidence that the structure was removed. No photos were found. Brief events (1965 replaced) match Canada Lookouts; no correction needed.
